title: RAG Evaluation
description: W10 metrics Stage 5 — the latest sanitized, offline batch RAG-evaluation run for each corpus (policy_corpus: db/policy_corpus_evaluate.py; patient_record_corpus: libs/rag_eval/harness.py), pushed opt-in via libs/rag_eval_metrics to the local Pushgateway. Never populated by an interactive request — only `make rag-eval-publish`. No query, answer, document, citation, or case identifier is ever in these series, only aggregate scores/counts. The Pushgateway holds NO persistent volume and is never seeded with placeholder/fake values: after any restart (or before the first-ever publish) every panel here is truthfully empty and the missing-evaluation/freshness alerts fire correctly, until `make rag-eval-publish` runs again.

panels.title: Recall@k / Precision@k / MRR by corpus
panels.description: rag_eval_mrr: mean reciprocal rank over runnable/gold cases — absent (not zero) when a corpus has no runnable case to rank at all. CAUTION: the two corpora use DIFFERENT retrieval cutoffs (see the rag_eval_top_k panel) — policy_corpus defaults to k=5, patient_record_corpus to k=1. A recall/precision/MRR value is only meaningful compared to another value at the SAME top_k; these two lines are NOT a fair side-by-side comparison of retrieval quality, only two independently-tracked trends sharing one axis/unit.

panels.title: Retrieval cutoff (top_k) by corpus
panels.description: The actual top_k each corpus's most recent evaluation was run with — read from that run's own report, never a value duplicated here. Different corpora legitimately use different cutoffs (policy_corpus: 5 by default; patient_record_corpus: 1 by default) — always check this before comparing recall/precision/MRR across corpora.

panels.title: Policy corpus: citation-target accuracy and negative-case retrieval safety
panels.description: rag_eval_negative_case_retrieval_safety_rate: fraction of unanswerable-by-design cases whose RETRIEVAL avoided every forbidden/unauthorized hit — see libs/rag_eval_metrics.negative_case_retrieval_safety_rate's docstring. This measures retrieval restraint only, NOT agent refusal-wording correctness (no agent runs as part of this evaluation).

panels.title: Policy corpus: forbidden citation / unauthorized retrieval
Patient-record corpus: duplicate rate / fragment-coverage gap
panels.description: AUD-09 identity-fragmentation effects on retrieval quality — see libs/rag_eval/metrics.py.

panels.title: Policy corpus: document/chunk parity and freshness issues
panels.description: expected_* comes from the current manifest; database_*/embedded_* from Postgres — a gap between them is exactly what freshness_issues_total counts.

panels.title: Evaluation age / freshness-check age by corpus
panels.description: Two INDEPENDENT ages, matching the two independent alerts: how long ago each CORPUS's last COMPLETED evaluation published (RagEvaluationStaleOrMissing checks policy_corpus and patient_record_corpus separately) vs. how long ago the policy corpus's freshness check last ran (RagCorpusFreshnessCheckStaleOrNotFresh). A stale/verify-only run advances only the second. A corpus with NO series here yet (a clean Pushgateway, or one that never published) is exactly the condition RagEvaluationStaleOrMissing's absent() branch catches.
